utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there are no preliminaries, we move into closed session in order to allow the witness to enter the courtroom, and we do that after Madam Registrar has called the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic will, as soon as the curtains are entirely up, will continue his cross-examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to start with part of a map of Sarajevo. We need 1D692 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is 1D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday we were discussing the incident at Alipasino Polje, the 22nd of February, 1994, is the relevant date. We had a look at a certain number of documents. And now we have in front of us part of a map of Sarajevo. We have marked the map with these red and blue lines. Would you agree that according to your findings the shell was fired from the direction of the institute for the blind, or rather, from territory that was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. That is how it appears according to the plan, the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that according to UNPROFOR documents the shell was fired from Butmir, the Upi [phoen] institute area, which is territory under the control of the ABiH. And this has been marked on this map with the red line.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the red line indicates direction from Butmir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember UNPROFOR's findings we had a look at yesterday? Would they agree to correspond to what they were claiming?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this was calculated yesterday, that would be the direction concerned, the south-west direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me, Mr. Lukic, what P exhibit it was so that I can select that for myself to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P exhibit -- it wasn't P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What D exhibit it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was 1D692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1D692. Has it not been admitted? No, I'm looking at the report you're referring to, UNPROFOR documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One second, please. It is 1D671.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it has not been tendered yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It hasn't. We used it and we would like to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, then do it right away. 1D671, no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receive number D177, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D177 is admitted into evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I think we have that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would it not be -- Madam Registrar, I hardly dare to say -- we thought we were at D178, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1D670 was admitted as D177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is supported by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I apologise. This is D178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D178 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we would like also to tender this, 1D692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, wouldn't it be good to finish your line of questioning, or is this your -- have you finished all your questions about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's been no foundation established through this witness that these markings are actually correct or correspond actually to the degrees that were measured. If it's just being offered for demonstrative purposes, and if fact that it's been shown to the witness, we have no objection. However, as to the accuracy of these markings there's been no foundation laid at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map only tells us that if they are fired from those positions, that this would be in the line of fire. It doesn't say anything about whether they were fired from there. Mr. Lukic, you agree, it just visualises what it would look like if it was fired either from the institute for the blind or from the Butmir-Ilidza source.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if the data in UNPROFOR analysis is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then it visualises what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing wrong with that. Madam Registrar, that would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D692 receives number D179, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. D179 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, I would now like to deal with the incident in Markale dated the 5th of February, 1994. We refer to that incident as Markale I here. You participated in the on-site investigation after the explosion of the Markale Market. When you arrived at the market -- when did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps an hour after the explosion, on the 13th or 14th [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The wounded and those killed had already been evacuated by that time; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had the various items also been removed from the stands or the stalls?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no. There were quite a few items there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 10468, which is a 65 ter Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this sketch? Does this depict the site at which there was an explosion in Markale?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this illustration, but I don't know who made the sketch. Yes, that is the Markale market-place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already answered my question. I wanted to ask you whether you knew who made this sketch; if you don't -- would you agree that the site of the explosion in the sketch doesn't correspond to the site referred to in official reports?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with this. Our measurements were different in our report, in our sketch, completely different. All I can say is the upper corner where the shell fell is more or less correct, but this distance of 6 metres is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that day what sort of investigative measures did you take?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our team headed by an investigation judge, Cano Carsic [phoen], I believe, and my colleague, Cavcic, and myself and Sead Besic as a forensic technician had the task to determine the direction of the shell and the type of shell that fell on the Markale Market. So we followed the standard procedure that I have already explained. This was the main task we had to carry out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You carried on with the investigation on the following day, on the 6th of February, 1994. Why did that happen? Why wasn't everything done on the 5th?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation that was carried out on the following day was launched again. I do not know for which reason because I did not participate in that investigation. We completed our part of the investigation on the 5th when UNPROFOR arrived. As you saw yesterday, they took the stabiliser out, and so on and so forth. But as to why and on whose orders a new investigation was launched, well, we could assume that the investigations judge asked for that because certain other judicial experts participated in the investigation. But I and my department were not involved in the subsequent investigation that was carried out on the 6th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see those findings? Did you determine that the co-ordinates for the explosion site were identical in your report and in the report of the commission headed by Mr. Berko Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the part that corresponded to our reports, the position of the quarter and the angle from the north of 18 degrees. That's where we assumed the shell arrived from. I wouldn't comment on any other elements. You would have to ask Zecevic about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that because of the shape of the site, of the explosion, it's almost impossible to obtain the same results when measurements are taken on different occasions, on two separate occasions? So would you perhaps have accepted Zecevic's findings or would he have accepted yours? That's the question I would like to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you seriously asking this witness whether Mr. Zecevic would have accepted the findings of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only one who can answer that question is Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe this gentleman accepted Mr. Zecevic's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was why I wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you asked both.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I can limit myself to this gentleman then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's one. And second, he said earlier that he would not comment on it, but of course you could give it another try but -- and acceptance or not, what we need is an analysis of the findings and a basis on which they were made. That is what we need. And whether then this witness would accept someone else's findings or someone else's -- the important matter is whether the Chamber accepts any of those findings on the basis of the information underlying those findings, but this witness by accepting or not accepting might give us some additional thoughts on the matter. Witness Sabljica, could you tell us whether you have reasons to accept or not to accept the findings? I do not know exactly which ones, but in a report, which report, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will -- Mr. Zecevic should come and testify here. We will have his report as well, the report produced based on the investigation carried on the 6th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we can do is to ask this witness whether he accepts the findings in report X, Y, or Z; that is, a report clearly identified so that the Chamber also is able to see what the witness accepts or does not accept. There may be a consultation. Apparently Mr. Mladic asked for it. If it can be very short, that is, at low voice, 30 seconds okay; not any more, otherwise it should be done during the break. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to take care of a quick housekeeping matter, I just wanted to put on the record that the document that was called up 10468 which is now on the screens has already been admitted as P538 on page 56 just so that we have that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I said 30 seconds, low voice. They are over now. If there's need for further consultations, the breaks will help you out. Mr. Lukic, again I do not mind if you ask the witness whether he accepts any findings, but then the Chamber should know exactly what you are referring to and the witness should also know exactly what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think we realise what the Chamber is interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The co-ordinates of the site of the explosion are identical in your report and in Mr. Zecevic's report. My first question is of an objective kind. Would you agree that it is almost impossible, especially because of the shape of the site of the explosion, to obtain two completely identical findings when measurements are taken on two separate occasions, on two different days?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you that it's not at all difficult to take those measurements because you determine the length and the distance from fixed objects, so you can always locate the centre of the explosion in relation to these surrounding buildings. So those are the distances concerned. So perhaps the margin of error that we are dealing with is a centimetre or 2, but this doesn't really affect the findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The points from which you took these measurements, were they the same in your report and in Mr. Zecevic's report? Do you remember anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which report, Mr. Lukic? The Chamber wants to be able to verify that, whatever the answer is and we would like to hear the answer. But we want to be able to verify reports, compare reports, verify answers. So could you please be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have that number here with me, but I'll try to provide it during the break. Then the next question I can ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you take the measurements or did you accept the measurements taken by Mr. Berko Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again are you pointing at measurements - which is well possible - the measurements from the centre of the crater to the surrounding buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or the altitude of those buildings? Or what are we talking about? The witness said that the measurements were the same and that the margin of error from the centre of the crater to the surrounding buildings would not be more than 2 centimetres, which is -- I do understand. Is that the measurements you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I keep asking about the co-ordinates or the grid references of the point of impact. That was contained in my earlier questions as in the latter ones. I'm referring to the co-ordinates of the point of impact, of the point of the explosion, and that they are the same in both reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then of course what I would like to do is to see how these co-ordinates are described. You can do it in two ways: Either you take a picture and you measure from a building what is the distance to the core of the centre of the crater; or you look at really grid co-ordinates. Grid co-ordinates are, by definition, not points but areas. And the more detailed the grid reference is, the smaller the area is. We would like to see what we are talking about because a grid reference is, well let's say, 1 metre by 1 metre or 10 centimetres by 10 centimetres; whereas if you measure from the centre of a crater the distance to a building, you can be as precise to 2, 3, or 4 centimetres, that's the -- even the witness said the margin of error is 2 centimetres approximately. That is the kind of things we would like to know in order to be able to interpret the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I'm not interested in figures at all. We have the figures. I'm interested in what kind of methodology was used by this gentleman. Did he measure the site himself or did he take the measurements that Mr. Zecevic had? What was the methodology used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's a different question, which is fine. It's a different question. If you say: Did you adopt measurements from others in their reports, then the only thing I would like to know is: Which report? So that I can see what measurements are in that report which then apparently were or were not adopted by this witness. Mr. Sabljica, meanwhile the question seems to be a different one. When you did your investigation, did you adopt any measurements from any report by Mr. Zecevic; and if so, which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us clarify this issue at once. The first time I saw Mr. Zecevic's findings was in 2001 as I was preparing for the Galic case. This means that we did our part of the job completely independently. I wasn't aware at the time that Mr. Zecevic was part of that team on that other day, and that's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. That's all I wanted to know at present. Let's go back to the day when you conducted your investigation. When you arrived at the scene was the market-place cleared up, that part of the market-place where you worked, where you did your work, was it cleared up or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was only the dead bodies that were taken away and the wounded that were evacuated, but there were a lot of items strewn around. There was a lot of blood, tissue, and I suppose other belongings of the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the police footage number P864 in the time sequence from 6 minutes, 43 seconds to 6 minutes, 48 seconds, we heard a voice say, Have a look up at the roof-top lest you should find the tail fin there. Will you agree with me that at the point of your arrival you were not aware that the tail fin was in the crater; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your practical work you had come across cases previously where the stabiliser had been embedded in the ground for its full length. Let's look at P867 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you just had 65 ter 10468 on the screen, the sketch you referred to. That is the separately uploaded page 56 of what is Exhibit P538, so as to be sure what we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And that's why -- yeah. But it's also the Prosecutor's number so we used this one because it was easier for us to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it was page 56 of Exhibit P538.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] We need the following pages from this document: In B/C/S, 26; the English version doesn't have as many pages or it only has text. That's not the page we need. Perhaps we should look at page 27. Can we do that, please. No, then 25, please. The numeration must be different in e-court. Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the tail which can be seen at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible for us to get a translation of what's written at the bottom of this picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, then we have to have the same, 25th page, of English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's go -- let's go for it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Lukic, we'll have a look at the text but you referred to words spoken on video P864.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, P864 was tendered and admitted but without a transcript. So I do understand that the Prosecution does not rely on any text spoken. Is that correct, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your quote from what was said at a certain moment in this video needs a transcript, which we can read and which can be verified by the Prosecution. Would you please keep this in mind because we are unable to verify anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll just do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then sort that out. Then we now look at the text underneath. We have it. Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe the corresponding English translation is just one page further on page 26 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this seems not to be the text related to this one. I take it the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if this is the stabiliser that was embedded in the ground at the Dobrinja incident site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the mortar stabiliser, mortar shell stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't need the text. Can we have a look at P864 from 7 minutes, 29 seconds, to 7 minutes, 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course I kindly ask Ms. Stewart for assistance. Can we have 7 minutes 29 seconds to 7 minutes 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You measured the hole and you established that it was 9 centimetres deep; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that yesterday. When the UNPROFOR officer uncovered the tail fin of the shell, we took the measurements at the time when it was still embedded in the ground. So the 9 centimetres is the distance between the surface of the ground and the surface of the tail fin. That's the 9 centimetres. When we took the stabiliser out we did not measure the depth of the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for everyone to be able to follow, this is P868. It is a record of the forensic examination of the site. And at page 15 of the B/C/S version and page 16 of the English version, the findings are related. Page 15 of the B/C/S version and 16 of the English. I'm stating this for the record only. We -- or at least I don't need to have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work, what were your conclusions? For the stabiliser to be embedded so deep in the ground, what sort of charge was needed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only have made an assumption, you know. We did not look into what the exact source of fire was. We know that a 120-millimetre mortar shell would have charge number 6 and we know that it was 18 degrees north/north-west, and I learned later on that there was six batteries located down there, one of which was the BH army's and the rest was the VRS's. I didn't make that analysis, and I think that question would be better put to those who analysed this in more depth and that's Zecevic and the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look briefly at P868. We need page 63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In which language?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In both languages. I think that we have picture only in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There it is in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please have a look at this and do you understand what this black-and-white ribbon represents at the bottom of the photograph, this black-and-white strip. Have you ever seen measurements taken of a shell on the basis of such a strip or by using such a strip?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This measuring strip is part of the equipment that a forensic technician uses. It's usually placed by the physical evidence. One of these rectangles or squares represents 1 centimetre. You probably know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are now -- we are having a look at this photograph. We claim that these rectangles aren't of the same size and that this was done in order to conceal certain evidence. Given the depiction here, what would the width be of this tail?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 120-millimetres would be the diameter, 12 centimetres, from one end of the fin to the other. If you look at it length-wise you know what a diameter is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We can see 13 fields here; isn't that correct? Well, it's not important. We now need to have a look at page 62 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you say it's not important. At the same time you express a suggestion that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But not on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the next [overlapping speakers] not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see in this photograph, this is, in fact, what I was talking about. In this photograph the black-and-white rectangles don't have the same size. So the intention was to claim that this was, in fact, bigger than it actually is. According to this photograph what would the length or height be of this item?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be about 22 centimetres if you add up these squares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to mistreat you now, but these black-and-white squares should be of an identical size; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Each one should be 1 centimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can I ask for clarification?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The picture on the right side generally looks bigger than the picture on the left side. It looks like it's more of a close-up than the other one. If you are saying the squares are not the same size, I'll say to you the stabilisers are also not of the same size looking at these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably we got it through the e-court. It's different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I think what you are -- but let me just try to understand Mr. Lukic. Is it your point that the black parts are not exactly of the same size as the white parts, irrespective of it being enlarged or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is exactly my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not the left picture to the right picture --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but the black boxes against the white ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then, if you say so, that's a different story. That's not what I understood you to be saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was unclear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Lukic kindly wait for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're asked to wait for the interpretation before you respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, on that occasion, given the number of victims, did you deal with the issue of whether there had been a number of explosions in Markale before the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our team didn't do that. We just focused on this shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P868, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- I have another question in relation to this photograph on the screen for the witness. Can you help me with the following: Where was this strip on the left side, black-and-white? Was that part of the photograph or is that part of the page in which the photograph is included? I mean was that near this object? How can I understand that? Because the left and the left edge of this piece of paper of this photograph is not exactly clear. Can you help me with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, the forensic technician always makes the photographs. He makes such photographs in his office after the on-site investigation, and this measuring strip is part of the equipment he uses. It's a plastic strip with 1-centimetre black-and-white boxes. And this photograph taken by my colleague, Sead Besic, is a photograph that he wanted to use to show what the length of this tail fin was. The difference in size of these boxes could be because he took a photograph from a certain angle, and so on and so forth. But this is a standard strip, but it would be better if you obtained information from him as to how he took the photograph and then Mr. Lukic will have a better idea of the procedure. I hope I have assisted you with this explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we take a break in five minutes. If there's a need for a longer consultation, we would even consider to take it a bit earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to tell Your Honours that the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Low voice, please. Low voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The report of Mr. Berko Zecevic we talked about earlier and I didn't have the reference is 65 ter number 10637.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome. [Interpretation] Now I'd like to see P868 on the screen. The pagination is the same in the B/C/S and English version, and I'd like to have a look at page 27. It's the same document. We only need to see the sketch, and I'd like to have a look at the lower left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You made this sketch of the site; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This is my sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there's a sketch of a stall with the standard measurements that you made here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a side view of a stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please focus on the awning which is at the top and to the right. It goes beyond the supporting pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we were on the right spot. We can keep that picture downward. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we would need to have a look at the video again, P864. The time is 1.15 to 1 minute and 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1 minute 15 to 1 minute 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I show something completely different, but anyways.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree - I'm not sure how clearly you can see things in what we have just viewed - would you agree that these awnings are a lot longer and that they screen the areas between them, close off these areas between them? Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're quite densely positioned. All you have is an opening for people and for trollies. I was interested in this sketch in widths here and in the side view of the stall. I wasn't really interested in the awnings of the stalls.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this sketch doesn't depict the actual look and size of the stalls in respect of the awnings?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The width is to 100 but the size or the shape of the stalls is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we'll have to have a break now when the Judges so order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can take a break. We first move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And until the curtains are up I use the time to say something about P612 which is the criminal investigation filed pertaining to a sniping incident. The Prosecution has provided a revised version of the English translation of this document and the Registry may replace the old English version with the new one. That's hereby on the record. Mr. Lukic, if you're ready you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, we've finished the issue of Markale. Would you now please focus on Dobrinja. The date is the 4th of February, 1994. It's the incident that happened one day before Markale. Let start with a couple of general questions before we move on to the events themselves. Would you agree with me that the methods used in your investigations could lead to only approximate findings.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. Only the trajectory, direction of fire, and type of projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again an unclear question. Not precise in respect of something the witness investigated? Or not precise because the witness did not investigate certain elements?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the methods used in your investigations could lead to only approximate findings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer of the witness was: "I agree. Only the trajectory, direction of fire, and type of projectile." The answer focuses on what could not be concluded because of the limited scope of the investigation. I got the impression that your question was about the methods used which might create a margin of error of, well, let's say 2 or 3 degrees. That is not part of the answer and it's unclear whether it is included in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard the Judge. Can you give an answer to what the Chamber is interested in?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The method used was one that was generally used, universally used for the parameters that I was interested in. We could never establish exactly where the fire was open from, and this is the shortcoming of that method but it was due to the difficult times we were in and the fact that there were things that simply we couldn't do. That's why in our findings we always said "plus/minus 5 degrees" as the margin of error with regard to the direction of fire. And that is the only method used for mortar shells to establish the direction of fire. Of course the source of fire is something that could never have been established by using this method.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also told us that you never examined the angle of descent, save for one incident, Livanjska Street at Kosevo hill, when the method used was the one of the stake. Would you agree with me that this isn't an official method for establishing the angle of descent? It isn't one that would be found in the professional literature?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's what we called it. But in principle it gives you the findings of the angle of descent through certain very precise method. The weight of the shell, the cosine of the angle, if you had the protractor which we had. And of course this stake of the rod was just there to facilitate our work. Of course we also used the margin of error in that respect. We stated what the margin of error was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 1D674 in e-court. It's a map showing one area of the town. It's Dobrinja again. Can we magnify the lower right-hand corner where it says "Dobrinja" just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you mark Mihajla Pupina Street on this map for us, please. Can you take the pen, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best. To the best of my recollection it would be roughly here. I'll put MP for Mihajlo Pupin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is called Zlatnih Ljiljana Square and it's actually now the combination of Mihajlo Pupina and Sose Street; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so. I know they've renamed many streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the direction where Lukavica lies and could you mark it with L for Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm approximising, but I think roughly there. The road that you see up there is one that leads to Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Hamdije Kapidzica Street, which is the former Nehru Street that you must be familiar with. That was where the police station was.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's assume it's this one, but I'm not 100 per cent sure and I'll put an N for Nehru. It's a small-scale map so there's not much I can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your effort. Can you mark for us on this same map the place where the explosion took place on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's these buildings here. Let's put an EX for "explosion." But that's all I can assume on the basis of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we save this map with the markings as the next Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so could we ask the witness -- you asked for the street with the police station. I take it you did not do it without reason. If the police station is relevant, I'd like to know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to mark for us on this map the location where you believe the police station was situated?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you asked me to, I marked the street, but I don't know exactly where it was on that street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection? If you would see the area, would you know where the police station was to be found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't know where the police station was exactly on that street during the war either. I never went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Do you have a clear recollection of the incident you said where you marked a building, do you have a recollection on where the explosive landed? Was it in between of houses? Do you have a recollection of that because then we could look in more detail from an aerial photograph to know exactly where it was. But we don't have to do it if your recollection would not serve you well enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that it was a playground of sorts, that it was surrounded by buildings, and that people were lining up for humanitarian relief. That's all I remember. When looking at the photo documentation during proofing I refreshed my memory somewhat. But I don't know the exact positions. As Mr. Lukic and I discussed yesterday Dobrinja was a precisely planned housing development, so they had these playgrounds inserted in between. Perhaps we could try and look at a better map but I can't say that with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest, Mr. Lukic, that we first have this one admitted and then look in a bit more in detail at page 30 of P3. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for the document 1D674 as marked by the witness will be D180, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. And could we have a look at P3 and then we'll move to page -- in hard copy, it is page 30 but we'll see what it is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe that's e-court page 35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thirty-five. Let's have a look at 35. And could the witness be assisted in marking. Could the usher assist the witness with a pen to mark. It is not very clear, I must say. If I look at the hard copy it's by far clearer. Is there any way we could -- could we make it brighter? Is there any way of doing that? That's not exactly -- now, Witness, the area which is approximately the same area as you marked -- but has someone -- I could give my hard copy to the -- could you give your hard copy for a moment, Mr. Weber, so that the witness is better able to orient himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sabljica, you see a bad reproduction of what is now given to you in hard copy as an aerial photograph of the Dobrinja area, where with a yellow marking the area of the impact is approximately indicated. Could you tell us a bit more about what you remember where that shell fell. Was it in the playground in the left part of the oval yellow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One landed in the playground, in the left corner of the yellow circle, and the other landed closer to the building which is in parallel to the playground. And people who were lining up for either water or humanitarian relief were injured. Two shells landed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent possible, could you make one little cross with a 1 for the first shell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be at that eastern edge of the stretch of that building. Then a little X with a 2 for the second shell -- oh, it's there already. Yes. And now for the place where people were queuing for humanitarian aid, could you make there a little cross with an H for humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Roughly like this. As far as the scale would allow me to. I tried to be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much for that. Mr. Lukic, we could make it a Chamber exhibit, but I'm happy to have it a D exhibit as well that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to inquire if the witness can recognise the police station now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I had in mind earlier, but he said he never visited it so he wouldn't know where it was. So whether an aerial photograph could help him out. On this photograph are you any better able to tell us where the police station was or would you still not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I don't know, unfortunately. I never went to that police station. I don't know where it is in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just before we admit it, just for -- if the witness can recognise the street [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but as a matter of fact, Mr. Lukic, the name of the street is in our P3 binder map and that's exactly where the witness indicated it to be. So the streets shouldn't be any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I'm not going to steal your evidence. It's yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- no, no, no, Mr. Lukic. Let's make it part of the cross-examination. Let's give it a D number. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness becomes Exhibit D181, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D181 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would now like to call up in e-court, once we have this photograph saved, to look at P867. In this document we need page 12 in both versions and that should be the page in e-court. I don't know why we have this, but we need page 11 in the B/C/S version then. Page 12 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, we have a report of a forensic examination of the site which concerns this incident of the 4th of February, 1994, the police station. It says the police station and then Novi Grad. Did this belong to Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it belonged to the municipality of Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under item 4, the forensic technician, Samir Selman, stated that three shells had been fired, three 120-millimetre shells had been fired on Dobrinja, on the Dobrinja settlement. He said that they fell in the street of Oslobodilaca Sarajevo and Dz Nehru Street. In the course of your work, did you know that these explosions related to the Dzevaharlal Nehrua Street in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this. In our findings which is in the table part of the document you can see what we noted but this is something you would have to ask Mr. Selman, Samir you said. You'd have to ask him about what he wrote here. I can't assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that day you didn't carry out any investigations in the Nehru Street; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We ballistics experts didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. In this report at the bottom it says a forensic examination of the site. In the B/C/S version, we have to move on to the following page. It's the same page, however, in the English version. It says that there were traces of a shell that were found under 6 that the tail fin of a shell had been found and a photograph was taken of it. It also says that traces of blood and tissue were also found. What it says here wasn't obtained on the basis of your work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not aware of this shell in Nehru Street. We didn't investigate this matter. If that is what the forensic technician had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Mr. Selmo? If so, did you see him at the site on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Selman. He was a member of the forensic technicians team and I believe that he was at the site with us that Zdenko Eterovic was the investigations judge. We can check this in the report. It says who the forensic technician was, but I do know Samir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is already an exhibit in evidence. In this very same document we need to see page 20 in both versions, the English version and the B/C/S version. I need to see a previous page. We'll deal with this one too, but I need to see the previous page or perhaps -- in fact, it's two pages back in the B/C/S, one page back in the English version. The pagination I have in the electronic version is a little confused. Can we go one page back in both versions. I do apologise for this confusion. We finally have what we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we can see that it says that the sketch of the site -- it says the sketch of the site, subject: Shelling, location Dobrinja, Oslobodilaca Grada. You said that you weren't familiar with Dobrinja, so I don't know where you could agree with me about the following, but according to the information I have there is no street that goes by this name in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, there's Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street. Samir Selman probably made a typo, a typing mistake, because he is the person who made this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll stay with the same document, but the e-court pagination isn't the same as the pagination I have. So we need to go three pages forward in the B/C/S version and we could have a look at the English version, too, for the sake of the text. Let's try and see page 21 in the e-court system. And another page forward. The next page, page 22. The page number I wrote down is page 23 but the pagination has been mixed up. This is the page I need. I apologise. Which page is this? I'm asking this just so I could follow, which page is it in e-court. Twenty-two, one page less. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is part of the photo documentation. Can you see this arrow?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is where one of the shells fell. Do you know which shell it is, what order it fell in?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about the order. All I know is when it was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here it also says, there is a mistake, that the plateau is between Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street and Nehru Street, the open area, in fact, is between these two streets. Is it correct that apart from the fact that it says Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street, it says that Nehru Street is in the vicinity. Is it true that Nehru Street is not in the vicinity of this site, this location, that we can see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bulevar Usoja [phoen] was there -- or rather, Mimara. I'm not sure what the name of the street is now. That's the street that were there, so -- Branjavaca Sarajeva [phoen] Street and Bulevar Usoja that leads towards Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how far is Nehru Street, roughly speaking? How far away is that street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an entire block of buildings. Perhaps a thousand metres away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Thank you. In this photograph, in this colour photograph on the screen, can we see the trace of earth on the asphalt surface which is a result of the impact of the shell? Can the traces of earth be clearly seen there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see a trace of dust, of earth. It's more visible now that you have enlarged the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Z for earth?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mark it with a circle and Z.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You do remember the site and you found traces of a shell here at this site; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the location marked with a red arrow. In the other photographs you can probably see the site more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number D182, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D182 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'd like to have a look at page 19 in this document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a sketch of the site where the shells struck - we'll deal with other ones too. Could you show us the direction of Lukavica on this sketch, in which direction is Lukavica located?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be difficult for me to do that on this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you can't do that, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the north. Lukavica was north-east of this site, but I can't really locate the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could the parties agree on it? We have clear maps and we know exactly what the spot is, so therefore it should be a very simple thing to indicate on this map where Lukavica is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know. It is not easy for me. I tried to use the witness list from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's the advantage of maps. We know where it is. We know exactly where it is. We know where Lukavica is on a map. You can draw a line, then you know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll try to talk with the Prosecution about that, Your Honour. Thank you. [Interpretation] I'd like to go one page back in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is part of the documents. It's referred to in that sketch of the site that we will get back to. It says there, in fact, that three shells struck and here it says that three 120-millimetre mortar shells fell on Dobrinja settlement and we'll return to the sketch to have another look at it and to see how it was marked. On that occasion did you launch an investigation into two shells or into three shells?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were investigating two shells. As you can see on the sketch we have marked the points of impact with the numbers 1 and 2. I assume that Samir made this sketch. And the third shell -- can you see the building across the road from the Oslobodilaca Grada, it should say "Sarajevo." As far as I can remember -- well, why didn't we deal with the third shell? Well, it hit a religious building that was used for Muslim rites. There were no victims. And this is why the two of us ballistics experts didn't investigate the matter after having consulted the investigative judge. I think that that is clearly stated in our findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. In that case I think that we will deal with the issue. There were also victims there too, wounded individuals. I'm still interested in the same exhibit. I would like to see page 26 now. It might be page 27 in the English version. I can see that it's one page back in the B/C/S version, although I have made a note of the fact that it should be page 27 in both versions. Yes. We can see the translation of the text beneath the photograph here, the English translation. Would you be so kind as to take a marker and mark the longer axis on this photograph, the site struck by the projectile at the point of impact. So the lengthier axis is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the longer axis of this irregular ellipse which is formed around the crater?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the axis of the descent of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: C for centre and X1 is the longer axis, which corresponds with the direction of fire and angle of descent. You can see that arrow there. If you want me to, I can mark the traces of the fan as it emanates outwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, what is the bearing of the north here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this direction here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we save this and mark it as the next Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number D183, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have this photograph with the text in B/C/S and another copy which has the English text only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Sabljica, it states here the site of impact of the mortar shell with a map of Sarajevo and compass on top used to determine the direction from which the shell came in. The arrow points to the east on the map of Sarajevo and that is where Energoinvest Lukavica is located, in that direction. Would you agree with me that you, in fact, marked quite the opposite of what is marked in this photograph, that, in fact, it's the arrow that points to the north and that's what the compass shows?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can that be? East is on your right if you face the north, and the arrow actually comes from the east and it is pointing toward the centre of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you explain what is it, what makes you believe that it would be opposite? I have difficulties in following your questioning --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and I'd like to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- on the other photographs we had arrow pointing to the direction of what is mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's east then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let's then -- an arrow has a tail and has a point. Do I understand that the question was about the white arrow on the map? Mr. Sabljica, could you confirm that the tail of the error is the direction from where the projectile came? Is that how we have to understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the tail of the arrow shows the direction of fire, and the tip of the arrow shows or points to the crater. In this case, the arrow indicates that the shell had arrived from the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may try to understand you, you said the tail of the arrows shows the direction of fire. What you, as I understand, intended to say is that the tail of the arrow shows the direction of the origin of fire. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The arrow points to the location from which the shell was fired and the direction from which it flew into the crater. In this case it's the east. That's what the arrow is there to denote. It points to the point of impact whilst its tail indicates the direction or the location from which it had been fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Mr. Sabljica ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry. Can you please indicate for us what is being said to be the arrow on this picture and which way it's pointing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll use the pen to draw it. This is where the north is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is not my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my question, Mr. Sabljica. Please, show me the arrow that is said to be on this picture. That's all I'm asking for. And show me which way it is pointing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've circled the arrow and it shows the direction from which the shell came and landed. So it was fired from the east --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From east.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- flying westward [In English] to west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have showed me. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there may have been some confusion with the letter 1 on the black shield whereas we were talking about the arrow, the white arrow situated on the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is very unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, we can see that the compass is quite close to the point of impact of the shell. Is it true that the remains of the shell present there may interfere with the way the compass works?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a good question. We did look into that issue and we examined it even in our lab. How do the metal objects lying near the metal needle affect it, but we concluded that there was no major interference. That's why they placed the margin error as plus/minus 5 since our conclusion was that there was no major influence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Mr. Lukic repeat his question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you please repeat your question because the interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the declination. Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I used the wrong term, I meant departure or deviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one additional question. Mr. Lukic assumed in his question that metal objects were lying near to the metal needle of the compass. Now, if a mortar shell explodes, would you expect a part, perhaps from a tail fin, but would you expect traces of pieces of metal or pieces of metal itself in the vicinity of the centre of the crater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer your question. Before applying this method --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. There seems to be a problem with the audio for Mr. Mladic. Has it been resolved, Mr. Mladic? Yes, I see that Mr. Mladic affirms that it has been resolved. You were to say that you could answer my question, "Before applying this method ...," yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there happened to be more fragments [Realtime transcript read in error "paramilitaries"] of metal at the scene, the forensic examiner has a duty to photograph these artefacts and then we start our work. In the conditions within the laboratory we -- we took measurements of how metal fragments may affect the magnetic needle, and we concluded that the tail of the shell and its scattered parts that were at the scene had no effect whatsoever on the magnetic needle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was a different one. After an explosion do the pieces of shrapnel usually stay close to the centre of the impact or would they usually fly away far from that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They will be scattered at greater distances. It is only rarely that you would find them close to the centre of impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If it is a convenient time for you, it is a convenient time for me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We move into closed session. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I can clarify it later if you'd like, but I just believe that there was an error in the transcript on page 42, line 12 , the first word of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, once the curtains have stopped murmuring, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I would now like to go back to these questions we were dealing with. Judge Orie asked you about these fragments of metal. Is it true that after an explosion the detonator of a shell remains in the crater and depending on the shell it can weigh up to 200 grams?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The detonator can often be found beneath the tail fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And often the tail fin is found there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have shell detectors?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of detectors? No, we didn't have such devices amongst our equipment. Our colleagues from the civilian protection did, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We mentioned the margin of error very briefly. I'm not going to maltreat you with this issue but is it true compasses had to be locked up from time to time in order to check whether there were any deviations in relation to the rules that were established? Did you have such conditions in war time to do such things; and if so, where did you do such things?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. They have to be locked up or sometimes they have to be calibrated to see what the effect of metal fragments on them is. We tried to keep them in a wooden box that didn't have any metal parts and was, so to speak, quite well sealed. So on the assistance of Zlatko Medilovic [phoen], the late, Zlatko Medilovic, who had a lot of experience, we tried to do such things under such difficult conditions. We tried to make sure that the compasses were, so to speak, taken care of, or well calibrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you yourself didn't calibrate them. You didn't lock them up anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the same document now, P867, page 23. Do you remember, is this the trace of the explosion of one of the shells on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to be the trace of the impact of a shell in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you or do you not remember whether this photograph was, in fact, taken on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember, but if it's an integral part of the documents I assume it has to do with the matter. You can see the entire area here where the shell fell and various items were marked, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 31 in the same document now. Page 30, I apologise. We'll move on. As I can't find the right page -- there it is. That's the page I was looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is also part of the photographs that relate to the case. Would it be possible for you to mark this photograph, to mark the approximate direction from which the shell arrived in this photograph and could you also mark the shrapnel on the wall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would suggest, yes, only to have that photograph on the screen and to be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now have a better view. Mr. Sabljica, would this be possible for you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be really difficult for me to do that in this photograph. It's very dark. I can only see these numbers, 7 and 8, so I would be doing no more than improvising and the results wouldn't be the results that we are hoping for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I accept that. In that case -- we don't need the photograph but it isn't bothering me. In the documents that relate to this case there are no photographs of the shell that hit the Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street of the site. But when you spoke to your colleagues did you find out why there was not a single photograph of the shell that fell in the Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we have noted, the forensic technicians compiled the documents. As I said, that third shell, according to the information we had and the information that the investigative judge had, hit a religious feature. There were no victims so we didn't launch an investigation. The judge decided that it wasn't necessary. I assume that's why there are no photographs of the event. But if the forensic technician appears, you will have to ask him why he listed the third shell in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would briefly like to move on to another incident -- in fact, not briefly. The incident in Livanjska dated the 8th of November, 1994. With regard to this incident, there was a conflict with UNPROFOR; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it a conflict, but difference in opinions or concerning the way the literature should be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't mean you had a fight. You had different opinions. There was a clash of opinions. Similarly -- if we could have a look at your report very briefly. P855 is the number. And we need to have a look at page 95 in the B/C/S version, page 59 in the English version. Here you were shown the document which we will later deal with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where are we exactly, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. This English is line 41 on 59th page and it goes up to 60, up to line 11. Let me check in English once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says you were shown a report from the MUP RBH and the SUP Sarajevo and it says that a shell was fired 20 degrees from the east, from the wider area of Spicaste Stijene, or sharp stone. And in your answer you say: "I immediately noticed a mistake. It says '20 degrees from the east.'" It should say, according to you, 20 degrees from the north towards the east. The report was compiled by Mr. Miokovic. And you also stressed that you did not agree with his assessment. The report drafted by the Sarajevo MUP isn't correct, at least as far as this part is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The Draganov's [as interpreted] report isn't correct in relation to the direction from which the shell came. I stand by that and you'll have to ask Dragan why he drew such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many shells were there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Three; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One at about 3.30 and the other two at about 5.30 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here you say that there was a clash concerning the method used. On this occasion did UNPROFOR determine that the 3.30 shell, the shell fired at 3.30, that's the one we'll deal with first, did they determine that it arrived from the position under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember with regard to the direction from which the shell came we were in full agreement. However, UNPROFOR had additional equipment which it used to determine the angle of descent and it also calculated the origin of fire, the approximate origin of fire, but they used firing tables for the artillery and they related to a Finnish artillery piece, or rather, a Finnish mortar, not the mortars used by the army. It was an 82- or 120-millimetre mortar from the JNA. I can't remember which one exactly. And they didn't deal with such a device. That was the reason for our disagreement. I remember that I personally gave the captain of UNPROFOR a book on that mortar in the CSB premises, and in that book he could find the firing tables, and so on and so forth, and that was the reason for the clash. And it's true that they determined one of the locations and said that one of the locations was possibly in the hands of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for the Chamber to form an opinion about these matters we have to know exactly what UNPROFOR report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're coming to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the report of MUP is P621.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you could already reveal what the number of the UNPROFOR report would be if you come to it soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have several UNPROFOR documents so I don't know which one exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you first move on but at least if at a certain moment we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The investigation was led by Dragan Miokovic. We've agreed on that point already. Can we call up in e-court 65 ter 28592.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P609, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
