utterances.text: [Interpretation] At page 3 we need P609 in e-court. Thank you to the registrar. [In English] It's P609.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is how Mr. Miokovic explains it at page 3 in both versions. The paragraphs are marked. We need paragraph 7. We're waiting for the English version to appear. This is what Mr. Miokovic had to say: "As a result of the conclusions at that meeting, I called the head of the local police station and asked him to order his policemen not to let anyone and UNPROFOR in particular to enter the site." Did you know that on that first day during the investigations access was denied to UNPROFOR members to the site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and this comes very much as a surprise to me. We always wanted people to join and work on the analysis. And when I say "we," I mean the forensics team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 at the bottom of the page, can we have it on our screens, please, it states: "On that same day on a press conference held by UNPROFOR at 8.00 p.m. that evening, a spokesman said to the journalists that Bosnian police had not allowed them to carry out ..." And we need to move on to the next page. "... to carry out on investigation." The text goes on to say: "On that same evening our Minister of Interior passed an order to prepare the report because it was requested by the Presidency of the State and I did." So you were not aware of the fact that UNPROFOR representatives did not attend this or were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know any of this, none of which you showed me was familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Likewise, if you remember, the on-site investigation was carried out outside of the presence of an investigating judge; is that right? We can see that in P621.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Because apparently the judge authorised Miokovic and that's his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we started looking at paragraph 7 which starts with: "As a result of the conclusions at that meeting ..." The meeting is described in paragraph 6 and expresses concerns that UNPROFOR would go to a site of an incident and then to remove evidence. And the last portion of paragraph 6 reads that although the police would not allow UNPROFOR to go there and remove anything, that we also agreed to let UNPROFOR investigate at the same time if they wanted to but without taking away the evidence, which sheds a totally different light on all of your questions, that is, they shouldn't go there first and take shrapnel and whatever there was. But they were welcome to participate or to join in the investigation when the police was active. So by reading paragraph 7 only and by referring to a press conference, the situation is more completely described if we include paragraph 6, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I will follow-up on your questions then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course but it would have been better for us before reading paragraph 7 that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- read all the documents we have but we don't have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic, but the context of paragraph 6 is of course of vital importance for the understanding of paragraph 7 and for the press conference. I leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, is it true that it was customary for UNPROFOR to take pieces of evidence, such as shrapnel, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were cases where they would take the tail fin of a shell to carry out their analysis, leaving us with empty hands. But when it comes to these statements you should ask Dragan about it. I can confirm that there were cases such as the one you asked me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this instance it was decided, as we can tell, that contrary to the customary practice of allowing UNPROFOR to take items away, they should not be allowed to do so here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that that was the case, but let me tell you that members of the forensic team that I was one of never took part in these discussions nor were we ever consulted about whether they should be allowed to attend or not. We were to do what our line of duty was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall any other time when you could not agree with UNPROFOR or you had a misunderstanding with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall a case which was not described anywhere. One shell landed at the airport in Sarajevo which was under their control at the time. They set up two teams, one of which consisted of members of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and another consisting of members of the MUP and Army of Republika Srpska. We were supposed to provide our expertise and findings as did UNPROFOR. I believe there was again a difference of opinion when it came to the origin of fire. I think the rest we could agree on. This is the only case that I can recall at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to refresh your memory, there was another difference of opinion on the 24th of October, 1994, when there was an incident at Pofalici close to the Orthodox church when the Bosnian side claimed that it -- fire had come from the VRS side, whereas UNPROFOR claimed that it was the BH side.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought you were asking me about shelling incidents. There were sniper incidents of that case. This was an incident involving a tram, I believe. And I think that I explained this case in the case against Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We should now see 1D685 which is one of UNPROFOR's documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just inquire with Mr. Lukic if this is the same document as P869.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: True. I didn't include the numbers, all of the numbers from yesterday. Some of them I do have, some I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you shed some light on whether this is P869.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe it's a different -- I believe the -- it's a different uploaded copy of the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, in order to keep -- to keep track of everything, would you be willing to work on the basis of P869?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's have P869 on our screens. Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, and if I'm wrong -- I just -- it seemed to be the same document so -- we're still confirming, but I was just inquiring with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it is the same -- if you check that then all the questions and answers relating to this document would apply similarly to the P exhibit and would -- perhaps at the end you could confirm whether this is the same or not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can tell that the document concerns Livanjska Street. Can you tell what the problem was on the basis of the document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem was the range of the mortar. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The members of UNPROFOR involved are French; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of them were French, and I think it was a colonel or lieutenant-colonel that was in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hereby put on the record that the first page of this document bears the same ERN number as P869. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your knowledge at the time based on the tables that they used - and you say that they were Finnish, right? - what was the charge contained, or rather, what was the charge of the shell in question? How many charges did it have?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they counted the basic charge and the six additional charges. According to -- if we compare it with the 82-millimetre mortar and the firing tables used by the JNA, theirs -- their range was 42 metres shorter. I believe that was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that in the annex here we received information to the effect that they had tables relating to the charges for the mortars produced in the former Yugoslavia. Let's look at it briefly. 1D686 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first establish on the basis of this report which finding that exactly is that -- there was a discussion about. I see it says here range between a hundred and 5.000 metres. Could we go back to the previous one. Is that what the discussion was about? I want to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I believe that question is addressed to you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I knew never saw the findings when they were done. We discussed the matter at the scene and I could tell that the representative of UNPROFOR used the firing tables that did not apply to the weapons used by any of the warring parties in Sarajevo. That was the cause of our difference of opinion and I didn't even want to go into establishing the source of fire because we had agreed on the direction of fire, the direction from which the shells came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we find the direction of fire in this report? Let me just have a look. The direction of the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- I don't know if we have it in this. We have it in P860 that we -- are we using that one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's disagreement about various aspects, I'd like to know what is written in this report. The conclusion is that: "It is possible to conclude that the most suspected area is on Serbian side, between Brijeg and Izlaze." But I was looking for the direction of the origin of fire. Is that on page 2? Because I didn't find it on page 1. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is my sincere apology. I may have added to the confusion. I did have a further study of Mr. Lukic's upload under 1D number and it does contain some additional pages. And so if [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I was very wise when I only referred to the first page having the same ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, those even appear different in the 1D number. I believe that he used some earlier-uploaded pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm surprised by that because I was looking at P869 which is a three-page document and this is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do we have on our screen at this moment, P869? Yes, that's a three-page document. If the other document is a different one, we should look at that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an earlier ERN on the first page of the Defence upload that ends in number 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And that was 1D685.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have a look at that document then again. Yes, I see a different document. It consists of nine pages. Mr. Lukic, I was -- where the witness said that the range of -- the direction of the origin of fire was agreed upon, do we know where is that found in this document? I see angle of approach --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Angle of descent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- according to the spread of the impacts, it's between 1200 and 1600 mils. Suspected axis is 1400 miliems which is the same of mils, and when we are working in NATO mils we are working in the system of 6.400 mils in the 360-degrees of the compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which brings it to close to east, a little bit north of east.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we're talking about as far as the filing of UNPROFOR is concerned. And you agreed on that, if I understand you well. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now we would like to see the next number in a row 1D686. I'm afraid it's in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In French.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's the same incident and in connection with the same document -- range of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, this is in French and it apparently gives information --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it says something about that it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's depending on an angle of approach probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it compares it with a previous study, but now with the tables apparently from the -- another source. So there must be a similar study or document. But let's -- let's move on. It looks but -- it looks as if this is a document which covers the area between 1200 and 1600 mils from the point of impact with an X on 1400 mils and then gives distances related to an angle of impact and angle of descent. That's what the document seems to be about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's how we understand it as well. And I would just like to ask Mr. Sabljica if he has ever seen this document and these markings actually and whether this was the sort of misunderstanding in between him and UNPROFOR members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never seen this document before. We tried to reach a verbal agreement - I'd like to repeat that - because I could also speak English, so it was possible for me to talk to them. After we'd agreed on the direction, they said they would elaborate on their report and then they said that the range determined was the one determined for a Finnish mortar but I never saw this table here which seems very accurate. I don't remember the numbers for an 82-millimetre device. I dealt with such matters over 16 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the right, does that come from the tables you provided them with or from tables of your own? I'm referring to the part where it says charge 1, 2, 3, 6 -- charge 1, 2, 4, 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness tells us he has never seen this before -- or had never seen this before. How could he possibly tell us then on the basis of what data it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was only thinking about the charge since the witness said that he gave one table to UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they used that one or different --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course you couldn't know that by heart. Now, what apparently this picture tells us - and it seems rather common - that if you know the angle of descent, if you know the charge used, and if you have the accurate firing tables, that you could tell for what charge, for what angle of descent it may have been fired from, approximately where, whereas this chart apparently does not take yet into account any difference in elevation or altitude between the firing position and the landing position. That's apparently what this document can tell us. Would you agree with that, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now see P622 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it comes up on the screen we'll see that it is an official report from the MUP, the Sarajevo security services centre dated the 9th of November, 1994, and this document relates to the incident we are discussing now. We can see that you are also listed as a member of the team. You are the penultimate name that appears here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to have a look at page 2 in both versions, but we're interested in paragraph 3 in the B/C/S version and paragraph 4 in the English version. This is what I would like to draw your attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 of the B/C/S version it says -- it's towards the bottom of the paragraph: "The experts of the MUP and the RBH Sarajevo determined that the shell had been fired 20 degrees to the east, probably from the wider area of Spicaste Stijene that was under aggressor occupation." Please remember that it says "20 degrees" here. We now need to see something so that we can compare this with document 12942 which is 65 ter document. We can see that the date is the same. This is a bundle of documents in fact that deal with the 8th of November, 1994. And we need to see the following pages. Page 8 in the B/C/S version and page 3 in the English version. It's a report on the criminal forensic investigation of the site under number 4. It says with regard to a shell, this 82-millimetre shell -- it says that it was determined that the shell came from a direction 15 degrees due north-east. So it was an 82-millimetre shell. We can see in these two documents from the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP that we have two different pieces of information. According to one of the documents, the shell came from a direction 20 degrees from the east and the other one says that it came from a direction 15 degrees due north-east. So the information is not the same; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course that's the case, but none of these reports is a ballistics report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But is it a fact that they can't be relied on, at least not as far as this part of the report is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. They're not at all relevant. When it comes to what needs to be determined, the trajectory and the direction of fire, you would have to ask the authors of these documents why they provided such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What should be taken to be the source of their information?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our ballistics report should be the source of their information. Usually the boys didn't want to wait for 24 hours, and as a result this sort of thing would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is -- your microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D184 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, I'm trying to follow it all. It seems that the two reports from the local police are at least close to each other, 20 degrees, 15 degrees. There is, however, a huge difference with the UNPROFOR report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, which is 70 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There seems to be the main difference of view. And since the witness said that he had agreed, although orally, on the origin of fire, the direction of the origin of fire, the report shows a clear difference of view in that respect. Do you have any explanation for that, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I have just said, I would like to see the ballistics report which is an integral part of the document. So usually the officials who work on violent crimes, such as Miokovic and the other person - I don't know who it was - who drafted the report, they should have waited for our official findings to be provided within 24 hours and then they could have based their conclusions on the actual findings and stated where this shell came from. And this is the explanation of the reason for which this discrepancy occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think you agreed with the UNPROFOR about the origin of fire, the direction of the origin of fire. Now, do you have any explanation as to why such discrepancy between the UNPROFOR -- the UNPROFOR 70 degrees which was not established by your services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that we agreed that the direction was from the north-east, and in our ballistics report we said that there was a margin of error of a certain number of degrees from the north. It indicated the north-east and UNPROFOR called it the Orah [phoen] exit, I think. And Miokovic and my colleague, these two officials as I have already said, drafted a report sooner than they should have. I really do not know how it is that they arrived at those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this very same document we have findings obtained from investigating the traces of the explosion. Let's see whether these findings are yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you could assist me in one way or another to find on one of the maps the Livanjska Street, that would certainly assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on Kosevo hill. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on Kosevo hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. Perhaps I can find it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 10 in the B/C/S version of this document. Page 11 in the B/C/S version, page 5 in the English version. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document? It says an on-site investigation and analysis of traces from the explosion. You didn't sign it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the report of the counter-sabotage team, KDZ, it's not our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. It's not yours. So we don't have your report in these documents, only the report from the anti-sabotage team. But let's have a look at page 12 in the B/C/S version. We'll -- it's still page 5 in the English version. Is that page 3 or page 5 that we have in the English version? We need page 5, at least the way I have my papers sorted. Oh, it's all right. It's the right page. We can see here that this document states that the angle of descent of the mortar projectile is also established, and you did say that you would take these measurements. Is my understanding correct, that the angle of descent was, in fact, measured by UNPROFOR because they had additional equipment, the equipment that was necessary for this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, how Mr. Jamakovic and his team took these measurements, I don't know. You would have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your team did not measure the angle of descent, did it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During one of the on-site investigations at Kosevo hill we used this stake or rod method, and then I told you that it was the dimension of the first crown from the centre, the dimensions between -- also in relation to the detonator and the weight of the projectile. That was something that we learnt later on that UNPROFOR had been using. Now, as for this team here, how they made their measurements, that's not something I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that for the first one the angle of descent is 62 degrees and the other two mortar projectiles, 67 degrees. Do you remember now, since we don't have your document - at least I don't have it here - what the values were that you obtained for the angle of descent in this case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I'd like to look at my report. It's a pity that I don't have it on the screen here. As for our findings and those of UNPROFOR, we largely agreed. The only problem was that they would then be using these firing tables and measuring the source of fire. I didn't want to enter into any arguments with them. We never aimed to establish the source of fire to begin with because we were simply not equipped enough to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you asked whether they measured the angle of descent themselves or whether they adopted them from --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- UNPROFOR, I see that the -- UNPROFOR comes to an estimate between 70 and 75 degrees, whereas this report is talking about 62 or 67. So they could not have taken them from UNPROFOR, I would think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was asking about Mr. Sabljica's team. This is a different team, it's KDZ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, then that is clear to me and he doesn't know. Mr. Sabljica, we'll turn into closed session in order for you to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, from what I found the Livanjska Street is a very long street stretching, from what I see on the map, more than 1 or even close to 2 kilometres. If there would be any way to agree with the Prosecution where number 36 would be, that might assist. Please proceed. Mr. Mladic has difficulties with the audio. Could he be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My apologies for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do you hear me, Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you but I don't hear interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could -- is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He's not getting the translation. He can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was translated already to us. We will resolve the matter. Channel 6 is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that as a routine apparently the audio for Mr. Mladic is returned to channel 0, whereas it should be at channel 6. Apparently the problem has been resolved. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are finished with the shelling incidents. I'd like to briefly address the sniping incidents. You speak about M84 as well and we've heard it on a couple of occasions as well that it says the sower of death. The M84 is a light machine-gun which was part of the regular arsenal of the JNA and was even weaker than M53 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, source where the witness is using M84, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have page 104 for B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 104 of what, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in English it would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I come back later to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. But for us to follow the evidence we really need to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted clarification about what kind of a machine-gun that is, and I'm not going to dwell on it anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The incident of the 9th of November, 1994, is one where you say yourself where it was impossible to establish the calibre of the weapons used because the projectiles were fragmented. Let's now move on to the incident of the 23rd of November, 1994. I'll tell you right away what was contentious here in the process to establish the truth. It was established that the bullet was fired out of a -- or rather, came through an open window, whereas the woman who was wounded claimed to have heard glass smashing. In our view, the bullet could not have come through an open window -- through the open window that was there. Rather, it should have come from elsewhere. Did UNPROFOR attend the investigation into this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you help me out a bit? It's the tram incident; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that UNPROFOR members were there, if that's the tram involved. Is it the one near the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you right away. The tram was between the faculty of philosophy and the museum.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that they had their own anti-sniping team, but they wouldn't be conducting the on-site investigation together with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, they were there at the scene but they didn't participate in the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they were not the -- it was a different team. They were the team that was there to protect the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I will not pursue this line of questions. Do you remember on the issue of this tram again, perhaps we can look at P614 to refresh your memory. You see that this is a report dated the 24th and deals with the incident which happened on the 23rd of November, 1994. According to the testimony of the woman injured, it was a burst of fire which injured her and her husband. Do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have refreshed my memory about the incident. I don't know anything about the statement of the injured woman. It's a matter of assessing things. It's a subjective matter whether you decide if fire was a burst of fire or not that you can gauge if you have military or police experience. We made our analysis on the basis of what we had at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see here that it says that the man was hit with three shots and the woman who was standing next to him was shot once. This is P614. Let's look at P619. Perhaps we'll find it more easily.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is what you're asking me, well it could have happened. We don't have our findings here. But if we found one or two entries, you say that it -- the bullets came through an open window but they would have hit some surface, perhaps, and then got fragmented; and as such, fragments would hit several persons. In that case, we would not rule out that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were all the incidents resulting in injuries defined as sniper incidents even if -- or regardless of whether there was a burst of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the terminology used in principle. If we were able to ascertain the type of weapons used, we would make a note of it. But that was impossible. Later on it was only after the integration, as I said yesterday, we found M84s which are quite peculiar. They have peculiar cartridges. We called this alley the alley of snipers and that's how then every incident which took place along that stretch was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me look through the documents I have with me. Had your investigation indicated at any point that in the territory under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina fire was opened on civilians by members of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am under oath and of course I will speak the truth. I had never had a single such case in my career.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These are all the questions I had for you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Weber, do you -- is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do have a few questions, but if I could just check one document based on the last question before I start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, today you were shown a previously marked map in relation to the shelling on 22 January 1994 at temporary transcript pages 2 and 3. During the questions it was asserted to you that certain areas were occupied by BiH forces. Do you recall these questions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the incident in Alipasino Polje that related to the children on sleighs. Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall those questions about that map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that Mr. Lukic asked me whether confrontation line was between Vojnicko Polje and Nedzarici and he asked me about the positions of the two respective armies. Is that what you're thinking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 9786 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm calling up before you is going to be an SRK regular command report from Stanislav Galic dated 20 January 1994. Did you see this report prior to your testimony during proofing?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw this report at the proofings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to focus your attention on section 1 of the report in regard to the enemy forces, which in this case would be the BiH forces. Do you see that this report discusses enemy activities and mentions the presence of opposing forces in four areas: Zuc, Ilijas, Hrasnica, and Sokolovic Kolonija?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zuc, Ilijas, Hrasnica, and Sokolovic Kolonija are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are any of --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wider area of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are any of these areas near Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that close. Zuc is close as to -- it's on the other side of the river, to the north of Alipasino Polje, but that's about 4 or 5 kilometres away as the crow flies. Ilijas is very far from that location, it's about 20 kilometres away. And Hrasnica and Sokolovic Kolonija are beyond the airport strip, that would be about 5 or 6 kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would it be safe to say that all four of these areas are more than 1 kilometre from the location of the shelling on the 22nd of January?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to section 3 of the report, please, in the English version. Mr. Sabljica, this report indicates that the positions in Nedzarici were held by the SRK. Do you see that portion? It specifically references the 1st Infantry Battalion of the Ilidza Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. The positions are held by the 1st Infantry of the Ilidza Infantry Brigade. That is the Army of Republika Srpska, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this area consistent with where you found the shells to have come from, the direction of fire, on the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is consistent. You saw the blue lines that Mr. Lukic pointed to on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if the Prosecution could please tender this exhibit. In terms of origin information, the report was recovered from the VRS Kozara barracks in Banja Luka on the 21st of June, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would object this time since this document is predated the incident by two days. We don't know what happened on 22nd. This document is discussing what happened before it was released, probably one day before. It's probably for 19th even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's probative of where the forces were located and where activities were going on near the time of the shelling incident, particularly the locations of the enemy forces and also the positions controlled by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Active positions immediately prior to, is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say if there are any other active positions of the enemy two days later or three days later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Madam Registrar, the number would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 9786 receives number P873, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Before we continue, Mr. Lukic, could I ask you to have a look at D00178 admitted today and could we have on our screens the various pages in the original and in the translation. Mr. Lukic, it's the first page which does not correspond this cover page. If we move on the right side of the screen to the second page, we there see a -- I was only asking for the second page, but there we see UNPROFOR document. Could we adjust the right side of the page, move on to the third page. There it seems that this corresponds with what is the first page in the other -- on the other side. If we could move on to the next page, there we find information material which is not found on any of the two pages in the other document. Could we have a look at the second page of the left part of the screen. The third page -- fourth page, please. Let me see. I am now really surprised. I have the English version -- I have an English version in e-court which consists only of two pages. What we need is to carefully compare what there is. What we looked at, as a matter of fact, I think was mainly the two pages with the details in English but let me check again. Yes, we have an original and a translation. The translation consists of two pages, whereas the original consists of five pages. Could you please compare that and sort it out what exactly that is that you wanted us to admit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And discuss this with Mr. Weber and then report back to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, let me first see whether my colleagues have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Bench has no further questions for you. Mr. Lukic, may I take it that the question put by Mr. Weber does not trigger any need for further cross-examination? Then, Mr. Sabljica, this concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having testified not for the first time before this Court and now before this Chamber. I would like to thank you very much for having answered all those questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench and I wish you a safe return home again. Before you leave the courtroom we'll turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Just to be sure, I just received hard copies of Exhibit P869 and 65 ter 1D00685. Although the one contains one copy, one version, of the other, 1D00685 is quite a different document and gives far more pages and information. Just for me to check, Madam Registrar, have we dealt with the admission of 1D00685? We have not. Then I take it, Mr. Lukic, that you want to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would like to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, the number would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for 1D685 will be D185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Is the Prosecution ready tomorrow to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 7th of February, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of February, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.15 p.m.,
